```
...
# Theming
...
## Token Convention


We use semantic background and foreground pairs. The base token controls the
surface color and the `-foreground` token controls the text and icon color that sits on that surface.


The background suffix is omitted for the surface token. For example, `primary` pairs with `primary-foreground`.


Given the following CSS variables:

 Copy[Image: Image]

`--primary: oklch(0`.205` 0 0`);`--primary-foreground: oklch(0`.985` 0 0`);`
The `background` color of the following component will be `var(--primary)` and the `foreground` color will be `var(--primary-foreground)`.

 Copy[Image: Image]

`<`div` className`=`"bg-primary text-primary-foreground"`>`Hello`</`div`>`
...
...
# Theming
...
## Theme Tokens


These tokens live in your CSS file under `:root` and `.dark`.


|  |
|  |
| background / foreground | The default app background and text color. | The page shell, page sections, and default text. |
| card / card-foreground | Elevated surfaces and the content inside them. | Card, dashboard panels, settings panels. |
| popover / popover-foreground | Floating surfaces and the content inside them. | Popover, DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, and other overlays. |
| primary / primary-foreground | High-emphasis actions and brand surfaces. | Default Button, selected states, badges, and active accents. |
| secondary / secondary-foreground | Lower-emphasis filled actions and supporting surfaces. | Secondary buttons, secondary badges, and supporting UI. |
| muted / muted-foreground | Subtle surfaces and lower-emphasis content. | Descriptions, placeholders, empty states, helper text, and subdued surfaces. |
| accent / accent-foreground | Interactive hover, focus, and active surfaces. | Ghost buttons, menu highlight states, hovered rows, and selected items. |
```

```
"use client";

import Link from "next/link";
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";
import { ComponentProps } from "react";

export const AppLink = ({
  href,
  className,
  ...restProps
}: ComponentProps<typeof Link>) => {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const urlPath = typeof href === "string" ? href : href.pathname!;
  return (
    <Link
      href={href}
      className={`${pathname.startsWith(urlPath) ? "text-red-500  outline-2" : ""} ${className}`}
      {...restProps}
    />
  );
};
```

```
"use client";
```

```
import Link from "next/link";
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";
import { ModeToggle } from "@/components/mode-toggle";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input";

const links = [
  { href: "/blog", label: "Blog" },
  { href: "/about", label: "About" },
  { href: "/catalog/nowosci", label: "Shop" },
];

export function TopNavigation() {
  const pathname = usePathname();

  return (
    <header className="flex items-center gap-2">
      <nav className="flex items-center gap-1">
        {links.map(({ href, label }) => {
          const active = pathname.startsWith(href);
          return (
            <Button
              key={href}
              variant={active ? "secondary" : "ghost"}
              nativeButton={false}
              render={
                <Link href={href} aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined} />
              }
            >
              {label}
            </Button>
          );
        })}
      </nav>

      <Input type="search" placeholder="Search" className="ml-auto w-56" />
      <ModeToggle />
      <Button>Login</Button>
    </header
```

_**Agent (copilot/claude-haiku-5.5)**_

**Przyczyna:** types/validator.ts nie jest plikiem, który Next generuje w tym miejscu. Next zapisuje go do `validator.ts` (w dev do `types`). Plik w `types` z pierwszego commita to kopia tego pliku, przeniesiona o jeden poziom wyżej. Import `../../src/app/page.js` jest poprawny tylko z `types`. Z `types` wskazuje poza projekt, więc TypeScript nie znajduje modułu, a przez to typ `__InvalidParamMatchingKeys` nie spełnia ograniczenia. `tsconfig.json` ma `include: **/*.ts`, więc `next build` sprawdza ten plik i przerywa się.

**Jak Next go przegenerowuje:** `next dev`, `next build` i `next typegen` zapisują do `types` (tsconfig dołącza `.next/types/**/*.ts` i `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts`). Nigdy nie piszą do `types`. Twoje `npx next typegen` (exit 0) zregenerowało poprawny plik w `types`.

**Stan obecny:** plik `types/validator.ts` jest już usunięty z working tree (git pokazuje ` D`). Nie ja go usunąłem. Po tym `tsc --noEmit` zwraca exit 0, a `npm run build` przechodzi i buduje wszystkie trasy.

**Do decyzji:** w `types` zostały jeszcze `cache-life.d.ts`, `root-params.d.ts` i `routes.d.ts`. To też śledzone kopie plików z `types`. Build przechodzi, ale mogą się rozjechać z wygenerowanymi wersjami. Mogę je usunąć (`git rm`)?
